tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Identify the largest disk not yet on its goal peg, clear any smaller disks that block it, move the largest disk to its goal, then recursively solve the remaining disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is off‑goal and has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while a smaller disk remains on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move k disks from a source peg to a target peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a stack of multiple disks must be relocated between pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a whole stack as if it were a single unit, without first moving the top disks away.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier extracts the last such list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving out a closing bracket or appending extra commentary after the list, so the parser cannot extract a valid move list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Replay each move from the initial state and confirm that the final configuration matches the goal before submitting.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move sequence, before output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Assuming the moves achieve the goal without checking, resulting in a final state that differs from the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer should consist solely of the move list; any surrounding commentary, headings, or formatting will be ignored by the parser.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory sentences or headings before the move list, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, confirm that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk being moved and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a large disk onto a peg where a smaller disk sits on top, creating an illegal larger‑on‑smaller placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk will later need to be placed there, unless you move the small disk away beforehand.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing the smallest disk on the goal peg before moving the largest disk there, without later moving it away.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, first relocate all smaller disks that sit above it to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while a smaller disk remains on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops before outputting any moves, often due to early termination or forgetting to generate the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate a complete move list; even if no moves are needed, output an empty list [] (but for this task a full solution is required).

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early, cutting off the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the entire move sequence before writing and ensure the final answer ends with a complete list; watch token limits.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to check the current top of the source peg before issuing a move.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a small disk on the goal peg before larger disks are placed, creating a blocking situation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Only place small disks onto the goal peg after all larger disks that need to be below them have been moved there.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not check the size ordering of the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
